policy: A routed distance between chosen anchors is not an independently established ghat length. A current whole-ghat length requires a ghat-specific source and matched start/end limits on the same road alignment. Historical ghat descriptions, project lengths, railway inclines and city-to-ghat distances are separately classified, never silently substituted.

notes: The same named ghat has 13.8 km and 23.0 km modelled sections across route variants. A single shared actual-ghat length is not established. Expressway, old NH48 and railway incline lengths must be distinguished.

The official tourism reference locates the ghat near Mulshi and Mangaon but does not publish matching entry/exit limits. The atlas's 30.0 km chosen-marker interval cannot be certified as the ghat proper, nor replaced with an unsourced shorter figure.

The NH965DD project to Varandha's district border includes a long approach; its chainage difference is not a ghat length. NDMA gives an approximately 18 km ghat-road reference, not the atlas's 10.0 km interval; independently matched current limits are missing.

references.context: Varandh Ghat, approximately 18 km, on the former SH70. This is a published ghat-specific reference, not the entire Pandharpur-Bankot road. Its limits have not been independently matched to the sampled interval.

notes: Historical Fitzgerald/Ambenali identity is supported, but town-to-town Mahabaleshwar-Poladpur distances do not establish the precise ghat-only limits of the atlas's 32.0 km interval.

The historical description names Dhankal, Khempse and Pophli. The atlas's 19.1 km markers are not independently matched to that complete crest-to-foot description. Karad-Chiplun's 58 miles is an entire connecting road, not the pass.

The Gaganbawada sources distinguish this branch from Karul, but no matching surveyed complete-ghat limits were established. Town-to-town and approach distances are not substituted.

NDMA gives an approximately 10 km ghat section. The parliamentary project combines disjoint sections: its 21 km total is not the ghat, and its 16 km portion includes the town-end scope. Neither replaces the ghat-specific reference or establishes mapped limits.

references.context: The Ghat Length row does not print its unit. Interpreting it as km is consistent with the separate 34 min at 30 km/h entries, but an inferred unit is not promoted to a certified current length.

notes: The sampled 22.1 km marker interval stays on the upland: the end is higher than the start in all three terrain products. The protected-monument record establishes the fort at Mirvel, not a coastward road-descent boundary. The mapped interval must not be presented as the ghat proper.

SH189 is documented, but a full Chandgad/Tillari/Dodamarg road or hydropower project length is not the mountain section. No independent complete-ghat endpoint match was established for the 8.2 km sampled interval.
The Goa PWD's Sankhali-Chorla route inventory is a corridor description, not the exact ghat-only interval. The 20.4 km model section remains unverified against independently defined pass limits.
Karnataka's hilly-terrain DPR portion and Goa's Anmod-Mollem project have different extents. They must not be substituted for or silently combined into the atlas's 19.5 km model section.
